analysis:
After the Nuclear Suppliers Group agreed on 6 September 2008 to adjust its guidelines to enable full civil nuclear cooperation with India, Prime Minister Manmohan Singh said the decision "marks the end of India's decades-long isolation from the nuclear mainstream and of the technology denial regime".

The NSG waiver followed the IAEA Board of Governors' approval of India's safeguards agreement on 1 August 2008, and preceded the US Congress's approval of the India-US 123 Agreement in late September and October 2008. India had been subject to nuclear trade restrictions since its 1974 test and the NSG's 1992 rule.

India subsequently signed civil nuclear cooperation agreements with several countries, though the operationalisation of some projects has been slow. The 6 September 2008 statement is reproduced verbatim in contemporaneous arms-control reporting.
